articles.title: Acute knee sepsis after intramedullary nailing of open tibial shaft fractures: a comparison of intra-articular and extra-articular approaches.
articles.authors: Jensen B, Challa ST, Wagner RK, Borgida JS, Grisdela P Jr, Daniell H, et al.
articles.population: Adults treated with intramedullary nailing for open tibial shaft fractures between 2010 and 2023
articles.outcomes: Acute knee sepsis, deep and superficial infection, reoperation, and nonunion
articles.take_home: Acute knee sepsis after intramedullary nailing for open tibial shaft fractures was rare overall at 0.7%. Although it occurred slightly more often with suprapatellar (intra-articular) nailing than extra-articular approaches (1.1% versus 0.5%), this difference was not statistically significant and the study was too small to draw firm conclusions about which approach is safer.

articles.title: Case report: distal pronation abduction ankle fracture.
articles.authors: Coscia A, Eichman J, Swany L, Ahn J, Bakshi N, Talusan P
articles.population: Patients with distal pronation abduction ankle fractures
articles.outcomes: Satisfactory outcomes with standard fixation techniques
articles.take_home: This case report describes a rare variant ankle fracture pattern with severe soft tissue damage and a comminuted fibula fracture. Standard fixation methods worked well, but surgeons need to be aware of the added complexity of this injury type.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors of recurrence for Pseudomonas aeruginosa-associated fracture-related infection following surgical treatment : a 12-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wu H, Yu S, Sun D, Wang S, Wang X, Fu J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa-associated fracture-related infections involving limb fractures
articles.outcomes: Infection recurrence rates, need for amputation, infection control following debridement and antibiotic therapy, and risk factors for recurrence
articles.take_home: About 1 in 6 patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bone infections experienced recurrence after initial treatment, with higher risk in those who had multiple previous operations, resistant bacteria, or took antibiotics for less than four weeks. Waiting more than ten weeks before initial surgery was associated with lower recurrence risk compared with earlier intervention.

articles.title: Comparison of anterior-only and combined anterior-posterior approaches for complex acetabular fractures.
articles.authors: Kaptan AY, Dolap MA, Gocer E, Demir M, Varol R, Bal T, et al.
articles.population: Patients with complex acetabular fractures (T-type, both-column, or anterior column with posterior hemitransverse)
articles.outcomes: Reduction quality, Harris Hip Score, Majeed Pelvic Score, post-traumatic arthritis, complications, transfusion requirements
articles.take_home: For selected complex hip socket fractures, surgery through the front alone can work as well as surgery through both front and back, provided the fracture can be properly aligned and held stable from the front. Getting good alignment of the fracture matters more than how many surgical approaches are used.

articles.title: Return to duty after suture anchor repair of thumb metacarpophalangeal ulnar collateral ligament injuries in active duty soldiers.
articles.authors: Lee J, Chung JI, Yun Y, Jeong C, Lee SM, Woo I, et al.
articles.population: Active duty South Korean military personnel with acute or subacute thumb metacarpophalangeal ulnar collateral ligament injuries
articles.outcomes: Pain (Visual Analog Scale score 0.5), function (Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand score 4.2), thumb opposition (Kapandji score 9.1), return-to-duty time (11.8 weeks), return-to-duty rate (94.3% within 3 months), clinical valgus stability, complications (one superficial wound infection, three transient sensory disturbances)
articles.take_home: Soldiers treated with suture anchor repair for thumb ligament injuries had good pain relief and functional recovery, with 94% returning to unrestricted military duty within three months. Complications were minor and resolved without further surgery.

articles.title: Occupational recovery after work-related AO Spine type A1 compression fractures: Association between treatment strategy and sick-leave duration.
articles.authors: Jorda-Gomez P, Saiz-Sapena N, Vanaclocha L, Barrios C, Vanaclocha V
articles.population: Adults with work-related AO Spine type A1 thoracolumbar compression fractures without neurological deficit
articles.sample_size: 70 patients (35 vertebroplasty, 18 orthopedic bracing, 17 spinal arthrodesis)
articles.outcomes: Sick-leave duration (time from injury to return to work)
articles.take_home: Patients who had a minimally invasive procedure called vertebroplasty returned to work much faster (median 62 days) compared with those treated with bracing (145 days) or spinal surgery (178 days). The treatment type chosen was the strongest factor affecting how quickly people could work again.

articles.title: Association of Resilience with Clinical and Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Operative Fixation of Pilon Fractures.
articles.authors: Litten RM, McIlwain RN, Alders AN, Asad S, Spitler CA, Johnson MD, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years and over with pilon fractures treated with surgery at a single Level I trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes including global mental health, global physical health, physical function, pain interference, depression and anxiety; clinical outcomes including reoperation, fracture-related infection, nonunion and amputation
articles.take_home: Patients with higher resilience (measured using a resilience scale) reported better mental health, less depression and anxiety, and better physical function in the months following pilon fracture surgery compared to those with lower resilience. These differences appeared early after surgery and continued over time.

articles.title: The Influence of Multiple Doses of Intravenous Tranexamic Acid on Transfusions and Complications in the Treatment of Fragility Hip Fractures.
articles.authors: Davis S, Solomito MJ, McCracken C, Kumar M
articles.population: Patients aged 50 years and over treated for fragility hip fractures (femoral neck, intertrochanteric, or subtrochanteric fractures)
articles.sample_size: 1,691 patients (632 no TXA, 551 single dose, 508 multiple doses)
articles.outcomes: Post-operative blood transfusions, venous thromboembolism, surgical site infections, and death within one year of surgery
articles.take_home: Tranexamic acid (a medication given by injection) reduced the need for blood transfusions in hip fracture patients, with a single dose being as effective as multiple doses. A single dose also had the lowest rate of blood clots, and there was no increase in other serious complications or death rates with TXA use.

articles.title: Clinical and patient-reported outcomes for bicycle and micro-mobility accidents: A prospective study with 12-month injury follow-up.
articles.authors: Mjaland O, Hesjevoll IS, Bjornskau T, Roise O, Garratt AM
articles.population: People injured in bicycle and micro-mobility device accidents in Agder County, Norway
articles.sample_size: 317 participants who completed baseline assessment (out of 460 eligible)
articles.outcomes: Injury severity, injury patterns, helmet use, recovery time, and health-related quality of life measured by EQ-5D-5L at baseline, 3 months, 6 months and 12 months
articles.take_home: Most bicycle and micro-mobility accidents cause injuries to the head and arms, with the vast majority of people recovering to their pre-accident health within 12 months. Only 3% of people had not fully recovered after a year, and overall quality of life scores improved beyond pre-accident levels.

articles.title: Robot-assisted fracture reduction and treatment outcomes in type III and IV fragility fractures of the pelvis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Xiao H, Zhao C, Cao Q, Sun Q, Ma Y, Jian Y, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and older with type III or IV fragility fractures of the pelvis
articles.sample_size: 115 patients (39 robot-assisted fracture reduction, 34 manual closed reduction with navigation-assisted fixation, 42 initial non-operative treatment)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative reduction quality (Matta criteria), 1-year functional scores (Parker Mobility Score, Barthel Index, EQ-5D-5L), mortality at 6 months and 1 year, and surgery-related complications
articles.take_home: Robot-assisted fracture reduction produced better quality fracture reductions and slightly better mobility at one year compared to manual reduction with navigation. However, there was no clear survival advantage to surgery over non-operative treatment, and most other functional measures did not differ significantly between approaches.

articles.title: Factors associated with U-type sacral fractures in geriatric patients: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Wong AW, Musick AN, Wagner RK, Lehle CH, Vise HS, van Weezenbeek MA, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years and over with sacral fractures
articles.outcomes: Factors associated with U-type sacral fractures, defined as bilateral fractures with spinopelvic dissociation
articles.take_home: About 3 in 10 older adults with sacral fractures had the more severe U-type pattern. This type of fracture was more common in patients who could walk independently before injury, had existing spinal degeneration, and sustained their fracture from minor or no trauma.

articles.title: Traumatic spinal injuries in a rural tourist area: Epidemiology, seasonal trends and implications for healthcare resource allocation.
articles.authors: Peppucci E, Ferlito D, Meletti L, Montalbetti A, Piras G, Bucpapaj R, et al.
articles.population: Patients with traumatic spinal injury admitted to emergency department in a rural tourist area near Como Lake
articles.sample_size: 132 patients (140 admitted, 8 excluded due to missing data)
articles.outcomes: Demographic data, spinal regions affected (cervical, thoracic, lumbosacral, multiple), treatment type (conservative or surgical), trauma mechanisms, seasonal variations in injury rates
articles.take_home: Traumatic spinal injuries were significantly more common during warm months, mainly due to increased sports injuries, suggesting that rural areas with high summer tourism and sporting activity should plan to have more healthcare resources available during these peak times.

articles.title: Stress displacement and surgical benefit in Beckmann 7-9 pelvic ring injuries: A retrospective multicenter analysis.
articles.authors: Achebe CC, Thorne T, Mau M, Higgins TF, Rothberg DL, Haller JM, et al.
articles.population: Skeletally mature patients with lateral compression type 1 pelvic ring injuries (Beckmann scores 7-9)
articles.outcomes: Composite of all-cause mortality, non-elective hardware failure or revision, or worsening ambulatory category
articles.take_home: In pelvic injuries with 12-16 mm of stress-induced displacement, surgery was associated with fewer deaths, hardware complications or walking difficulties compared with nonoperative care. However, the researchers noted this finding was based on a small subset and requires further validation before changing clinical practice.

articles.title: Longitudinal radiographic comparison of percutaneous and open pedicle screw fixation for thoracolumbar burst fractures: A two-year follow-up study.
articles.authors: Wung CH, Chang CY, Hsu CC, Wu RW, Yang FS, Lu ML, et al.
articles.population: Patients with thoracolumbar burst fractures treated with short-segment posterior fixation
articles.outcomes: Cobb angle, lumbar lordosis angle, intraoperative blood loss, operative time, postoperative hospital stay, revision surgery
articles.take_home: Percutaneous pedicle screw fixation resulted in less bleeding during surgery and better spinal alignment at two years compared to open surgery, although both methods produced similar results during the first year. Neither approach required revision surgery during the two-year follow-up.

articles.title: Surgeon-performed iliac fascia catheter versus epidural analgesia versus no regional analgesia after anterior acetabular fracture surgery: A retrospective comparative study of 85 patients.
articles.authors: Bouffier V, Greze J, Villaret C, Veloso M, Sanchez C, Boudissa M, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing anterior acetabular fracture repair surgery
articles.sample_size: 85 patients (31 with surgeon-placed iliac fascia catheter, 30 with epidural analgesia, 24 with no regional analgesia)
articles.outcomes: Cumulative morphine consumption over first three postoperative days, daily morphine consumption, visual analogue scale pain scores
articles.take_home: The surgeon-placed iliac fascia catheter did not significantly reduce opioid pain relief compared to epidural analgesia or no regional analgesia after acetabular fracture surgery, though all groups had low pain scores and similar morphine use. The technique is simple to do during surgery but needs a randomised trial to confirm its value.

articles.title: Predictors of long-term quality of life following operative treatment of unstable pelvic ring injuries: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Ramesh P, Imran A, Nair MS, Devendra A, Chandramohan A, Dheenadhayalan J, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients with unstable pelvic ring injuries (AO/OTA 61B and 61C) treated with surgery
articles.outcomes: Health-related quality of life measured using EQ-5D-5L at mean 6.7 years follow-up. Mean quality of life score was 0.87 out of 1.0. Poor fracture reduction (>10 mm gap) and polytrauma were independently linked to worse long-term quality of life.
articles.take_home: For patients treated surgically for unstable pelvic fractures, achieving good fracture alignment during the operation is important for better long-term quality of life. Those who also had injuries to other parts of their body tended to have worse quality of life outcomes.

articles.title: Epidemiology, AO morphology, and diagnostic delay of discontinuous thoracolumbar fractures: A 10-year single-center cohort study.
articles.authors: Zeng Y, Tu C, Zhu L, Hu X, Shi H, Lv L, et al.
articles.population: Patients with discontinuous thoracolumbar fractures treated at a single centre between 2016 and 2025
articles.sample_size: 186 patients with discontinuous thoracolumbar fractures (from 4394 screened patients with spinal fractures)
articles.outcomes: Epidemiological features, AO morphology classification, fracture distribution patterns, and time to diagnosis of initially missed fractures
articles.take_home: Discontinuous thoracolumbar fractures are often missed on initial assessment, with nearly half of second fractures overlooked at first but recognised within 24 to 48 hours. These injuries tend to occur at the thoracolumbar junction and lower back in high-energy trauma and require careful systematic review of spine imaging.

articles.title: Prognostic value of baseline RDW-CV in critically ill patients with pelvic fractures: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Huang H, Gu L, Lu W
articles.population: Adult patients with pelvic fractures admitted to intensive care
articles.outcomes: 30-day, 90-day, and 365-day mortality; patients with elevated RDW-CV (>15.5%) had higher mortality at all timepoints compared to those with normal RDW-CV
articles.take_home: A blood test measure called RDW-CV taken when patients with serious pelvic fractures arrive in intensive care can help predict which patients are at higher risk of dying. Patients with elevated RDW-CV had roughly 2-3 times higher risk of death compared to those with normal levels.

articles.title: Increase in fracture-related infection in open distal femur fractures treated with locally delivered antibiotics.
articles.authors: White AB, Serbin R, Gambuzza M, Yu Z, Seymour RB, Wally MK, et al.
articles.population: Patients with operatively treated open distal femur fractures
articles.sample_size: 44 open fractures (24 with local antibiotics, 20 without)
articles.outcomes: Fracture-related infection (primary outcome); estimated blood loss, operative time, and reoperation (secondary outcomes)
articles.take_home: This study found that open distal femur fractures treated with locally delivered antibiotics had a higher rate of infection (about one in five patients) compared to those without local antibiotics (about one in twenty patients), which was unexpected and suggests local antibiotics may not help prevent infections in this type of fracture. The result was not statistically significant, so more research is needed to understand this finding.

articles.title: Nutritional optimization for older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery: a randomized controlled pilot trial.
articles.authors: Jodoin Z, Almeida G, Allegretti AL, Jakkaraju S, Serra M, Zelle BA
articles.population: Older adults aged 65 years and over undergoing hip fracture surgery
articles.outcomes: Study feasibility (recruitment, retention, compliance), reoperation, readmission, mortality, grip strength, quality of life, medical complications
articles.take_home: Nearly all older adults with hip fracture had nutritional deficiencies before surgery. The study design proved workable but needs changes to reduce patient drop-out rates, particularly by improving visit frequency and transport support.

articles.title: Intramedullary nailing compared with primary total hip arthroplasty for pertrochanteric fractures in autonomous elderly patients : a prospective randomized study.
articles.authors: Piercecchi A, Bordet A, Labattut L, Maczynski A, Baulot E, Martz P
articles.population: Autonomous elderly patients aged 70 years or older with pertrochanteric hip fractures
articles.sample_size: 69 patients (35 intramedullary nailing, 34 total hip arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score at six months (primary outcome), functional recovery, pain, complications, and mortality up to 4.1 years median follow-up
articles.take_home: Both intramedullary nailing and total hip arthroplasty gave similar functional results and survival in older people with pertrochanteric fractures, with no clear advantage to doing a hip replacement instead of internal fixation.

articles.title: Effect of exercise on bone health in middle aged and older adults: hierarchical network meta-analysis of randomised trials.
articles.authors: Lu C, Li L, Zhang L, Gao Q, Meng J, Xue Y, et al.
articles.study_type: Hierarchical Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Adults aged 40 years and older (middle aged 40-60 years and older adults over 60 years)
articles.sample_size: 124 trials with 18,429 participants (26 trials with 11,132 participants for fracture analysis)
articles.outcomes: Changes in bone mineral density at lumbar spine, femoral neck, and total hip; incidence of fractures
articles.take_home: Brisk walking or jogging and combined aerobic-resistance exercises probably help maintain bone density in middle aged and older adults. About 2-3 hours of brisk walking or jogging per week may provide meaningful benefits for bone health, whilst mixed aerobic and mind-body exercise may also help reduce fracture risk.

articles.title: Occupational injuries among orthopaedic surgeons in Greece: A cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Zampetakis K, Dimitriou R, Alpantaki K, Chaniotakis C, Tsioupros A, Ritzakis N, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons in Greece
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of occupational injuries, types of injuries, anatomical regions affected, impact on work, reporting behaviour, and risk factors
articles.take_home: Three-quarters of Greek orthopaedic surgeons reported occupational injuries, most commonly sharp object injuries, psychological strain, and hand and wrist problems. Most injuries were not formally reported, and few surgeons had received ergonomic training, indicating a need for better prevention strategies.

articles.title: A structured three-step reduction strategy for locked posterior fracture-dislocation of the proximal humerus through a standard deltopectoral approach: A retrospective case series.
articles.authors: Jiang Z, Xiang Y, Lei C, Fu Q, Huang M, Zhi XS, et al.
articles.population: Patients with acute locked posterior fracture-dislocation of the proximal humerus
articles.outcomes: Fracture union, avascular necrosis, recurrent dislocation, implant complications, range of motion, Constant-Murley score, subscapularis function
articles.take_home: A structured three-step reduction technique using an anterior approach successfully treated all 16 cases without need for additional procedures, with all fractures healing and no cases of avascular necrosis or recurrent dislocation at follow-up. Patients achieved good functional outcomes with average Constant-Murley scores of 85.4 and preserved shoulder strength.

articles.title: Prehospital transfusion requirements in severe trauma: A multicenter, retrospective estimate of requirements.
articles.authors: Thabouillot O, Narcisse J, Girard A, Raphael V, Rozenberg E, Wolff D
articles.population: Severely injured trauma patients transported to major trauma centres or undergoing resuscitation for traumatic cardiac arrest in Paris region
articles.sample_size: 139 patients meeting inclusion criteria (from 5921 prehospital missions)
articles.outcomes: Proportion meeting criteria for prehospital blood transfusion (ABC score ≥2 and intervention time >20 minutes); receipt of tranexamic acid; prehospital deaths and cardiac arrests
articles.take_home: About one in five severely injured trauma patients in this French study would have qualified for prehospital blood transfusion based on clinical scoring criteria and transport times. The authors suggest that prehospital blood transfusion should become a more routine consideration in advanced trauma services rather than remaining rare.

articles.title: Predictive factors for outcomes in pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis: a 10-year analysis of 341 patients.
articles.authors: Idarrha F, Demnati B, Boumediane EM, El Khir YF, Aziz S, Benhima MA, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients treated for pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis at a tertiary university hospital
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes assessed using Strickland and Glogovac criteria, DASH scores, and grip strength. Excellent or good outcomes in 68.9% of patients. Amputation required in 11.4% of cases.
articles.take_home: Early presentation and prompt treatment are critical for better outcomes in this serious hand infection. Patients with diabetes, delayed consultation, advanced disease stage, or infection from multiple bacteria have significantly worse functional results.

articles.title: Can you FORCE research implementation? A PERUKI survey to evaluate knowledge translation of the FORCE study.
articles.authors: Jenkins M, Bennett JF, Roland D, Perry DC
articles.study_type: Cross-sectional survey of knowledge translation and implementation
articles.population: Clinicians in paediatric emergency departments across the UK and Ireland
articles.outcomes: Awareness of FORCE trial findings, adoption of recommended torus fracture management, barriers and enablers to implementation
articles.take_home: Most clinicians knew about the FORCE trial, and over half changed their practice to use soft bandages or no immobilisation for children's forearm torus fractures after the trial was published. Using practical dissemination tools and peer influence helped clinicians adopt the new approach, whilst colleague and parent expectations often got in the way.

articles.title: Beyond surviving: The mental and physical impairment of health-related quality of life after polytrauma emphasizes the need for interprofessional long-term aftercare.
articles.authors: Spering C, Bator F, von Steinbuchel N, Neubert A, Awan Malik H, Lehmann W
articles.study_type: Single-centre retrospective cohort study with prospective data collection
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years or older who survived polytrauma (multiple serious injuries)
articles.outcomes: Health-related quality of life measured by SF-36, depressive symptoms (PHQ-9), anxiety symptoms (GAD-7), pain levels, daily functioning, and socioeconomic outcomes including employment status
articles.take_home: Two years after major trauma, most survivors have significantly reduced quality of life with persistent pain, physical difficulties, and mental health problems including depression and anxiety. Only about half returned to full-time work, and many needed better coordinated long-term support combining physical rehabilitation, mental health care, and help with returning to work and social life.

articles.title: Association of polyethylene type with revision and dislocation risk following primary total hip arthroplasty: a population-based cohort study from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Chabaita M, Iljazi A, Sorensen MS, Eriksson F, Overgaard S, Petersen MM
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision, dislocation, and cause-specific revision (dislocation, infection, aseptic loosening)
articles.take_home: Highly cross-linked polyethylene was associated with lower risk of hip dislocation and revision in larger implants (32 mm and 36 mm femoral heads), with the strongest benefits seen in 36 mm implants. No differences were found for smaller 28 mm implants.

articles.title: Age-specific TBSA thresholds for pediatric burn complications: A 13-year single-center inpatient retrospective cohort.
articles.authors: Hilewitz D, Har-Shai L, Keller A, Bal M, Hayun Y, Meshulam-Derazon S, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 0-18 years admitted to a tertiary paediatric centre with acute burns
articles.outcomes: Fever (≥38.5°C), ICU transfer, surgery, and in-hospital infection
articles.take_home: The study identified age-specific burn size thresholds to help predict which children are at higher risk of complications like needing intensive care or surgery. Younger children may need ICU consideration at lower burn sizes (around 8-10% of body surface area) compared to older children (around 15%).

articles.title: Surgical management of complex humeral shaft fractures (AO/OTA 12-C): A multicenter comparison of open plating, MIPO, and intramedullary nailing.
articles.authors: Yoon YC, Song HK, Oh HK, Cho WS, Kim JW
articles.population: Adults with complex humeral shaft fractures (AO/OTA type 12-C)
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union rates, complications (nerve palsy, nonunion, malunion), operative time, blood loss, and functional scores (DASH, MEPS, range of motion)
articles.take_home: All three surgical techniques for complex upper arm bone fractures achieved similar healing and functional results. Minimally invasive plating required less blood loss and shorter surgery time than open plating, though differences in long-term outcomes were not statistically significant.

articles.title: Patellar fractures: To plate them all? Results of a new treatment protocol.
articles.authors: Davidson A, Harats E, Levy Y, Stavsky M, Lieberman I, Altergot A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with surgically treated patellar fractures
articles.outcomes: Major complications (fixation failure or deep infection), minor complications (superficial infection, limited knee movement, persistent pain, stair-climbing difficulty), hardware removal rate, range of motion, cost
articles.take_home: Plate fixation for kneecap fractures reduced serious complications from 15% to 4% and meant fewer patients needed their hardware removed later (8% versus 26%). Patients who had plates fitted also had better knee movement and function, though plates cost about £6400 more overall.

articles.title: Sex differences in martial arts injuries presenting to emergency departments in the United States from 2015 to 2024.
articles.authors: Hamstra-Wright KL, Kremer H, Coumbe-Lilley JE, Khosla S
articles.population: People presenting to United States emergency departments with martial arts injuries
articles.outcomes: Sex differences in martial arts injuries by age, body region, diagnosis, and martial arts style from 2015 to 2024
articles.take_home: Women had a higher proportion of injuries in younger age groups and experienced more foot, hand and leg injuries and strains and sprains, particularly from striking-style martial arts. Men had higher injury rates from grappling and mixed martial arts, especially after 2020.

articles.title: Open versus percutaneous fibular graft harvesting in long bone nonunion surgery: A comparative cohort study.
articles.authors: Hseinat LA, Al-Bataineh M, Migdad AA, Aolymate M, Sbaihat M, Badaineh AAA, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing non-vascularised fibular grafting for long-bone non-unions
articles.outcomes: Postoperative pain scores, analgesia requirements, donor-site complications (particularly peroneal nerve sensory deficits), harvest time, blood loss, incision length, union rates, graft incorporation, and functional recovery
articles.take_home: Percutaneous fibular graft harvesting causes less pain after surgery, requires shorter operating time, and leads to fewer nerve problems compared to the traditional open method, whilst achieving similar healing outcomes. Both techniques successfully healed the bones without compromising safety.

articles.title: Evaluating the physical examination and diagnostic workup for occult Neck Of Femur fractures in a district general hospital.
articles.authors: Maksoud A, Nkala M, Henderson K, Minijenahalli-Narayanaswamy S
articles.population: Patients with suspected occult neck of femur fractures presenting to a UK district general hospital
articles.sample_size: 143 patients (131 imaging requests analysed after exclusions)
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity and specificity of physical examination tests (hip log-roll, straight leg raise, axial loading, heel percussion) compared to CT and MRI findings; diagnostic accuracy of a 4-point risk score combining clinical tests with age and gender
articles.take_home: Physical examination tests like the hip log-roll and straight leg raise are good at identifying patients who might not have a fracture, but are less reliable at confirming one. CT scans detected nearly all occult neck of femur fractures, and combining physical examination findings with a patient's age and gender improved the accuracy of deciding who needs imaging.

articles.title: Digital Stop The Bleed(R) training compared with in-person Stop The Bleed(R) training: Human instructors needed to demonstrate psychomotor skills.
articles.authors: Salisbury I, Manzanero S, Santomauro C, Pearce S, Young J, Young R, et al.
articles.population: Layperson participants
articles.outcomes: Knowledge scores, wound packing success, tourniquet application success, self-efficacy ratings
articles.take_home: Digital Stop the Bleed training taught the knowledge and theory as well as in-person training, but people trained digitally were less successful at the practical skills of wound packing and tourniquet application. This suggests digital training should be used alongside, not instead of, instructor-led training where people can watch and practise the physical techniques.

articles.title: Major trauma centre clinicians: who cares? A comprehensive study of major trauma centre clinicians: are they prone to increased levels of stress, burnout and secondary trauma symptoms?
articles.authors: Johnson L, Loonat S, Harwood PJ, Vollans SR
articles.population: Orthopaedic and vascular consultants working in Major Trauma Centres and general orthopaedic consultants not in MTCs
articles.sample_size: 20 consultants (11 MTC orthopaedic, 4 MTC vascular, 5 general orthopaedic)
articles.outcomes: Burnout, compassion fatigue, perceived stress and secondary traumatic stress scores; identified stressors and coping strategies
articles.take_home: Consultants working in Major Trauma Centres experience higher levels of burnout, stress and secondary traumatic stress than those in general orthopaedic practice. They cope best with workplace support from colleagues and through hobbies and exercise at home.

articles.title: Epidemiology of mountain bike-related injury presentations to emergency departments: A 15-year retrospective analysis.
articles.authors: Course G, Sharman JE, Zhao T, Otahal P, Tran V
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of hospital emergency department records
articles.population: People presenting to Tasmanian public hospital emergency departments with mountain bike-related injuries
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of presentations, clinical urgency levels, ambulance arrivals, hospital admissions, mortality, injury types and locations, and patient demographics
articles.take_home: After purpose-built mountain bike trails opened in 2015, emergency department presentations for mountain bike injuries increased threefold, with more severe cases requiring ambulance transport and hospital admission. Most injuries were to the arms and hands (51%), with fractures being the most common type (42%), and children aged 10-14 years showed the largest increase in injury rates.

articles.title: A national analysis evaluating epidemiology of traumatic e-scooter injuries: injury patterns, helmet use, and alcohol intoxication.
articles.authors: Othman Y, Nasef Y, Indorewala Y, Nishida C, Kata A, Hus A, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric and adult patients with e-scooter injuries
articles.outcomes: Injury patterns, mortality, ICU admission rates, hospitalization duration, helmet use, alcohol intoxication prevalence
articles.take_home: E-scooter injuries are rising sharply, with most patients experiencing mild to moderate injuries from falls. However, head and neck injuries caused nearly all deaths, and very few people wore helmets or avoided alcohol when riding.

articles.title: Impact of operative intervention in blunt cerebral vascular injury.
articles.authors: Taheri BD, Girish DV, Fajolu OD, Malgor RD, Rizzo JA, Dengler BA, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis using national trauma database
articles.population: Patients with blunt cerebrovascular injury from a national trauma database
articles.sample_size: 65,171 patients with blunt cerebrovascular injury out of 9,369,340 total encounters
articles.outcomes: Stroke rates, survival to discharge, injury severity scores
articles.take_home: Patients who had surgery for blunt cerebrovascular injury were more severely injured overall and had higher stroke rates (14% for endovascular procedures, 10% for open surgery) compared to non-surgical patients, but survival to discharge was similar between the two groups.

articles.title: Change associated with enoxaparin prophylactic anti-Xa levels during prolonged hospitalization in trauma patients.
articles.authors: Mangan LE, Gendron J, Seamon MJ, Martin ND, Lamore RF
articles.population: Trauma patients admitted to hospital requiring prolonged stays (over 14 days) and receiving enoxaparin blood clot prevention
articles.outcomes: Change in anti-Xa levels between first and repeat measurement at least 6 days later; incidence of blood clots and bleeding during hospital stay
articles.take_home: About one in four trauma patients on prolonged hospital stays showed significant changes in their blood clot prevention medication levels when rechecked after at least 6 days, mostly becoming too low. The study suggests that patients may need their medication levels monitored and adjusted regularly during long hospital stays, though larger studies are needed to confirm this.

articles.title: Epidemiology, functional outcomes, and socioeconomic burden of hand tendon injuries: A five-year retrospective cohort study in southern Italy.
articles.authors: Delia G, Colonna MR, Di Blasi F, Maruccia M, Lagana P, Genovese C, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent surgical repair of hand tendon injuries
articles.outcomes: Grip strength (mean 87% of expected), range of motion (mean 76% of expected), work absenteeism (mean 69.5 days), functional recovery by finger and tendon type
articles.take_home: Extensor tendon injuries were more common than flexor injuries, and patients who had postoperative rehabilitation showed better functional recovery than those who did not. Hand tendon injuries resulted in significant time off work, with employed patients taking about 81 days off compared to self-employed patients taking about 42 days.

articles.title: Emerging intraoperative diagnostic modalities for fracture-related infection: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Bessems L, Meuris A, Onsea J, Alt V, Verhofstad MHJ, Zalavras C, et al.
articles.study_type: Scoping review of intraoperative diagnostic techniques
articles.population: Patients with confirmed or suspected fracture-related infection, and experimental models
articles.sample_size: Seven studies included in the review
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic accuracy and performance of frozen section analysis and fluorescence-based imaging techniques for detecting fracture-related infection during surgery
articles.take_home: Current methods for detecting infection during fracture surgery have limitations, with frozen section analysis showing mixed results depending on the situation. Newer fluorescence-based imaging techniques, particularly using vancomycin-based tracers, look promising but need larger clinical trials before they can be recommended for routine use.

articles.title: Are Staphylococcus aureus fracture-related infections clonal, and what are the implications for bacteriophage therapy?
articles.authors: Doub JB, Nebeluk N, Tallon L, Hand R, Vavikolanu K, Santana-Cruz I, et al.
articles.study_type: Laboratory study of bacterial samples from patients with fracture infections
articles.population: Patients with Staphylococcus aureus fracture-related infections
articles.sample_size: 15 S. aureus fracture-related infection isolates (8 colonies sequenced per isolate)
articles.outcomes: Genetic similarity of bacteria within individual infections, bacteriophage activity against isolates, variation in genes related to bacteriophage attachment
articles.take_home: The study found that S. aureus bacteria causing fracture infections are clonal (all from one source) within each patient, with consistent genetic makeup and bacteriophage receptor profiles. This suggests that testing a single bacterial sample may be enough to predict how bacteriophage therapy would work against that patient's infection.

articles.title: Comparison of outcomes based on treatment type for geriatric acetabular fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Halvachizadeh S, Starr AJ, Bell L, Pfeifer R, Osterhoff G, Hoch A, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 55 years or older with acetabular fractures
articles.sample_size: 2703 patients from 20 studies (2034 treated with ORIF, 417 with primary THA or combined hip procedure)
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score and Oxford Hip Score, 90-day and 1-year mortality rates, reoperation and conversion rates
articles.take_home: Elderly patients who had hip replacement as their first treatment for acetabular fractures had better hip function at three months and needed fewer follow-up operations than those who had bone-fixing surgery first. However, the initial surgery took longer and involved more blood loss.

articles.title: The Birmingham Eye Trauma Terminology - Extension from Lebanon (BETT-XL) classification: A multi-center validation in modern warfare.
articles.authors: Ibrahim R, Arafat O, Mansour R, Sadaka A, Al Ghadban F, Nemer A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with ocular injuries from 2024 pager explosions in Lebanon
articles.outcomes: Ability to classify severe eye injuries including traumatic evisceration, luxation, avulsion and exenteration; comparison of BETT versus BETT-XL classification systems
articles.take_home: The new BETT-XL classification system can categorise severe eye injuries from modern warfare that the standard BETT system could not previously classify. In the Lebanese pager explosions cohort, over 24 to 34 percent of severely damaged eyes were unclassifiable using standard BETT but were captured by BETT-XL.

articles.title: Decision-making in patients facing limb salvage versus amputation after lower extremity trauma: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Engel R, Landon E, Bell E, Erdman MK, Beederman M
articles.population: patients with major lower extremity trauma facing limb salvage versus amputation decisions
articles.outcomes: psychosocial and clinical factors influencing patient decision-making; barriers to informed shared decision-making
articles.take_home: Patients facing the choice between saving or amputating a badly damaged leg are affected by emotional responses like grief, thinking biases and decision fatigue, which can be made worse by brain injury or pain medication. Better support through trauma-informed communication and structured decision aids may help patients make choices that align with their own values.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary management of fractures in patients with hemophilia: Advances in perioperative hemostasis and functional restoration in the era of novel therapies.
articles.authors: Wu K, Zhao L, Yu Z, Guo JJ
articles.population: Patients with hemophilia undergoing orthopaedic surgery for hemophilic arthropathy
articles.outcomes: Perioperative safety, surgical complications, functional outcomes after orthopaedic intervention
articles.take_home: This review summarises how new clotting factor treatments and coordinated care between multiple medical teams have made surgery safer for people with hemophilia who need joint operations. The key to good outcomes is careful planning beforehand, personalised treatment based on each person's bleeding risk, and proper rehabilitation afterwards.

articles.title: Success rate variation between trauma video review and chart review of trauma intubations at a Level 1 trauma center.
articles.authors: Ruderman A, Shanks C, Kernen R, Thakur B, McDonald S, Succar B, et al.
articles.population: Adult trauma patients requiring endotracheal intubation in the emergency department at a Level 1 trauma center
articles.outcomes: First pass success rate for intubation; comparison between video review and chart review methods; interrater reliability
articles.take_home: When doctors watched video recordings of trauma intubations, they found a 78% success rate on first attempt, which was lower than the 92% reported in medical charts. This suggests that video review may give a more accurate picture of how often intubations succeed on the first try than what is recorded in charts.

articles.title: Progress in multiscale biomechanical assessment of cancellous bone: From bone density to multiscale mechanical phenotypes.
articles.authors: Quan Y, Zhang X, Yang Z, Wang H, Xu J, Lv H, et al.
articles.population: Cancellous bone tissue
articles.outcomes: Comparison of assessment methods across macro-scale, meso-scale, and micro-/nano-scale techniques for evaluating bone mechanical properties and quality
articles.take_home: Standard bone density measurements only predict fractures with about 60% accuracy because they do not capture the full picture of bone quality. New multiscale assessment approaches that examine bone structure and composition at different levels offer more accurate ways to predict fracture risk and plan personalised bone surgery.

articles.title: Loading conditions during femoral preparation for THA procedures: Mechanical effects of broach holder offset.
articles.authors: Bridoux T, Zot F, Germaneau A, Vendeuvre T, Odri GA, Severyns M
articles.population: Femoral bone specimens
articles.outcomes: Cumulative force, mean force, maximum force, and number of strikes needed to seat broaches during hip replacement surgery preparation
articles.take_home: Using an offset broach handle required significantly more strikes to insert the broaches compared to a straight handle, although the total force applied was similar. Surgeons using offset handles would need to apply larger forces with each strike if they want to complete the procedure in the same time.

articles.title: Dislocations after hip hemiarthroplasty for acute femoral neck fractures: a scoping review.
articles.authors: Narhi SCF, Rasmussen LE, Rogmark C, Overgaard S, Viberg BL, Hermansen LL
articles.population: Patients with femoral neck fractures treated with hip hemiarthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Dislocation rates, risk factors for dislocation, and patient-reported outcomes following dislocation
articles.take_home: Hip dislocations after hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures occur in about 2 to 3 per cent of cases, with higher rates in older studies. Risk factors include cognitive impairment, certain hip shapes, and using a posterior surgical approach, which should be avoided where possible.

articles.title: Do ECG abnormalities, degree of sternal displacement or troponin level influence outcomes following sternal fracture?
articles.authors: Yeoh C, Ellis DY, Foo N, Hercus C, Petrakis N
articles.population: Patients with sternal fractures presenting to a Level 1 Trauma Centre
articles.outcomes: Mortality rates in relation to sternal displacement severity, troponin levels, and ECG changes
articles.take_home: Patients with moderate or severely displaced sternal fractures and elevated troponin levels had higher mortality rates and should be monitored closely. ECG abnormalities were also associated with increased mortality risk.
